advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Extend the MCP error guard (_mcp_errors._envelope_error) to recognize rebar.config.ConfigError so transition_ticket/claim_ticket surface the unreadable-config fault as a structured envelope, mirroring the CLI boundary added in this diff.
evidence: Diff adds CLI boundary: `except ConfigError as e:` / `sys.stderr.write(f"Error: {e}\n")` in src/rebar/_cli/__init__.py

MCP guard only matches known rebar exceptions: `if isinstance(exc, (RebarError, CommandError, mismatch_type, llm_error_type)):` — src/rebar/_mcp_errors.py:56 (returns None otherwise → original exception re-raised unwrapped)
ConfigError is not in that vocabulary: `class ConfigError(ValueError):` — src/rebar/_config_coercion.py:20; and `class RebarError(RuntimeError):` — src/rebar/_errors.py:19 (disjoint hierarchies)

MCP transition_ticket calls `rebar.transition(...)` (src/rebar/_mcp_writes.py:259) and claim_ticket calls `rebar.claim(...)` (src/rebar/_mcp_writes.py:289), both of which now raise ConfigError per the diff's _lib_writes.py docstrings
advisory.finding: The unreadable-config ConfigError now raised by rebar.transition/rebar.claim is given a clean operator rendering on the CLI boundary (_cli/__init__.py adds `except ConfigError`) but the sibling MCP write surface was not updated: the MCP structured-error guard (_mcp_errors._envelope_error) recognizes only RebarError/CommandError/ConcurrencyMismatch/LLMError, and ConfigError is `class ConfigError(ValueError)` (disjoint from RebarError(RuntimeError)), so a ConfigError raised inside transition_ticket/claim_ticket escapes the guard with no structured error_envelope.
scenarios: An MCP client invokes transition_ticket or claim_ticket against a repo whose rebar.toml cannot be parsed; the driving agent receives an unwrapped ConfigError with no structured error_envelope to branch on, unlike every other known rebar failure on that surface (and unlike the CLI, which now renders `Error: ...`).
advisory.suggested_fix: In src/rebar/_mcp_errors._envelope_error, include ConfigError in the recognized set, e.g. import `from rebar.config import ConfigError` and add it to the isinstance tuple: `isinstance(exc, (RebarError, CommandError, mismatch_type, llm_error_type, ConfigError))`, choosing an appropriate error code via error_code_for.

blocking.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm the new ConfigError-on-unreadable-config behavior of rebar.claim/rebar.transition is release-noted as an intentional behavior change (operator ruling 39f8-ae7c).
evidence: _lib_writes.py docstring update: 'Raises :class:`rebar.config.ConfigError` ... when the rebar config cannot be read while resolving a ``verify.*`` gate ... This changed in that ruling: previously an unreadable config fail-OPENed the opt-in gates and the transition proceeded.'
gates.py:113-118 now `raise ConfigError(...) from exc` where it previously returned GateState.UNREADABLE with a stderr warning

Consumer callsite: src/rebar/_commands/close_precheck.py:564 gates.gate_enabled(...) propagates; src/rebar/_commands/gates.py:196 and :282 propagate — reaching rebar.claim/rebar.transition public entrypoints
blocking.finding: Public library entrypoints rebar.claim/rebar.transition now RAISE rebar.ConfigError on a present-but-unreadable rebar.toml where they previously proceeded (fail-OPEN skip). This is an unversioned behavior change to the public library contract: input (a corrupt config file) that previously produced a successful claim/close is now rejected. It is intentional (operator ruling 39f8-ae7c) and documented in docstrings, but external library callers relying on the prior fail-open behavior will see new exceptions.
